[RESPONSE] I’ve been having really upsetting dreams, flashbacks, and intense anxiety—especially around loud noises, like those I heard in Iraq. These started about 7 weeks ago, shortly after I returned from active duty there three months ago. I’m constantly on edge, can’t sleep well, and feel guilty about things that happened during deployment. I’ve been avoiding places that remind me of the conflict—like the shooting range—and lately, I’ve even been refusing to leave my house unless my wife persuades me. Because of all this, I had to take a leave from my job as an army instructor, and I’m really struggling to adjust back to life at home.

Major Depressive Disorder is comorbid in ~50% of PTSD cases and shares overlapping features (anhedonia, sleep disturbance, guilt), but the trauma-triggered, cue-specific reactivity (e.g., to loud noises), flashbacks, and avoidance of trauma reminders are more specific to PTSD and less characteristic of primary MDD. Adjustment Disorder is less likely because symptoms exceed expected stress-response severity and duration, and impair function profoundly—beyond what is typical for adjustment. GAD is unlikely as the anxiety is tightly anchored to trauma cues (not generalized or free-floating), lacks chronic pre-deployment onset, and includes hallmark PTSD features (intrusions, flashbacks, trauma-specific avoidance) absent in GAD."}
